{"id": "20:10/q07", "question": "Why did Moses tell his family to stay?", "turns_on": "Whether the departure is explained by deliberate care for the family or an overwhelming response to the sight.", "positions": [{"id": "20:10/q07/p1", "position": "He wanted them to remain while he went to seek fire or directions.", "reasons": "Al-Ālūsī says he prevented them following him toward the fire, as people commonly do; Ṭabāṭabāʾ supplies an omitted promise to go and return. Al-Qushayrī stresses his care for them despite the valley's danger."}, {"id": "20:10/q07/p2", "position": "The sight drew him out in an agitation he could not resist.", "reasons": "Al-Qushayrī gives this as another account."}]}
{"id": "20:10/q08", "question": "How is the pronoun vowel in 'to his family' read?", "turns_on": "Pronoun dialect and phonological explanation; the sources agree that both vocalizations are transmitted.", "positions": [{"id": "20:10/q08/p1", "position": "The hāʾ is read with ḍamma.", "reasons": "Hamza is consistently named, also for 28:29; Ibn Mujāhid adds Ibn Saʿdān from Isḥāq al-Musayyabī, while Abū Ḥayyān and al-Ālūsī add al-Aʿmash, Ṭalḥa and a Nāfiʿ transmission. Al-Naḥḥās calls it original wāw retention and a dialect like marartu bihu; al-Jishumī describes transfer of the hamza vowel; al-Samīn calls it an original Hijazi dialect and reports an assimilation explanation. Qirāʾāt-Er offers dialectal leveling or syntax."}, {"id": "20:10/q08/p2", "position": "The hāʾ is read with kasra.", "reasons": "The other readers or majority are named by Ibn Mujāhid, al-Jishumī, al-Ṭabrisī and Abū Ḥayyān; al-Jishumī explains it through adjacent sukūns."}]}
{"id": "20:10/q09", "question": "What does 'ānastu' convey?", "turns_on": "Whether the verb highlights clear reassuring sight in this scene or the broader act of finding or sensing.", "positions": [{"id": "20:10/q09/p1", "position": "I saw distinctly or perceived clearly.", "reasons": "Ibn Qutayba cites 4:6 for the related sense recognized; al-Ṭabarī derives it from uns and cites an Arab proverb; al-Mubarrad describes distant reassuring sight and a hunting bird noticing prey; al-ʿAjjāj and al-Ḥārith ibn Ḥilliza furnish poetic usage. Al-Rāzī contrasts visible human beings with hidden jinn. Bint al-Shāṭiʾ counts four Moses-fire uses and a fifth at 4:6, and argues for familiarity or comfort rather than neutral sight; Iṣlāḥī says attentive observation."}, {"id": "20:10/q09/p2", "position": "I found or sensed something, potentially by a sense other than sight.", "reasons": "Al-Ṭabarī and al-Farrāʾ gloss found; al-Māwardī allows sensing something by a fire. Abū Ḥayyān and al-Samīn say perception is broader than sight and cite a verse about faint sound; dictionaries cited by Bint al-Shāṭiʾ include hearing."}]}
{"id": "20:10/q10", "question": "Why does Moses emphasize that he has seen a fire?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "20:10/q10/p1", "position": "He reports certain perception to reassure his family while leaving the hoped-for benefits uncertain.", "reasons": "Al-Bayḍāwī contrasts certain sight with merely hoped-for fire and guidance; al-Ālūsī says inna confirms the sight even though the family expressed no doubt. Ṭabāṭabāʾ takes the singular emphatic report to imply the others did not perceive the fire."}]}
{"id": "20:10/q11", "question": "How is the first-person yāʾ of 'innī' read?", "turns_on": "Whether the possessive yāʾ is opened in connection or kept quiescent.", "positions": [{"id": "20:10/q11/p1", "position": "It is read open, innīya.", "reasons": "Ibn al-Jazarī names the two Medinese, Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr among five yāʾs in this passage; Qirāʾāt-Er says the change affects prosody without changing meaning. Ibn Mujāhid reports that Nāfiʿ opens the listed first-person yāʾs except in walī fīhā and akhī ushdud; Abū ʿAmr excepts walī fīhā and ḥashartanī aʿmā; Ibn Kathīr excepts walī fīhā, yassir lī amrī, lidhikrī in, ʿalā ʿaynī idh, and biraʾsī innī. Each opens the remaining listed yāʾs."}, {"id": "20:10/q11/p2", "position": "It is read quiescent, innī.", "reasons": "Qirāʾāt-Er presents the quiescent form as the contrasting reading. Ibn Mujāhid reports that Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, Ibn ʿĀmir, and ʿĀṣim through Abū Bakr keep all the listed first-person yāʾs quiescent."}]}
{"id": "20:10/q12", "question": "Why does Moses say 'perhaps'?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "20:10/q12/p1", "position": "A firebrand or guide was hoped for, not guaranteed.", "reasons": "Al-Rāzī says Moses would not promise what he could not guarantee, contrasting a claim that Abraham lied for a good purpose. Al-Zamakhsharī, al-Bayḍāwī, al-Nasafī and al-Ālūsī distinguish the uncertain outcome from the certain sight."}]}
{"id": "20:10/q13", "question": "How is the yāʾ of 'laʿallī' read?", "turns_on": "Opening or quiescence of the first-person yāʾ.", "positions": [{"id": "20:10/q13/p1", "position": "It is read with fatḥ, laʿalliya.", "reasons": "Ibn al-Jazarī names Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Jaʿfar across six occurrences; Qirāʾāt-Er says meaning is unchanged. Ibn Mujāhid says Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr, and Ibn Kathīr open the listed first-person yāʾs apart from their individually named exceptions; laʿallī is not among those exceptions."}, {"id": "20:10/q13/p2", "position": "It is read quiescent, laʿallī.", "reasons": "Ibn al-Jazarī names the Kufans and Yaʿqūb; Qirāʾāt-Er contrasts it with open yāʾ. Ibn Mujāhid reports that Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, Ibn ʿĀmir, and ʿĀṣim through Abū Bakr keep all listed first-person yāʾs quiescent."}]}
{"id": "20:10/q14", "question": "What is the 'qabas' Moses hopes to bring?", "turns_on": "Whether qabas is specifically a flaming brand, as al-Ālūsī insists, or may also be called an ember.", "positions": [{"id": "20:10/q14/p1", "position": "A flame or burning brand taken from a larger fire, carried on a stick or wick for warmth.", "reasons": "Al-Farrāʾ, al-Ṭabarī and al-Zajjāj specify the tip of a stick or reed, and al-Zajjāj allows a wick; al-Samīn calls it a passive-sense verbal noun, a glowing end taken up. Al-Ālūsī equates it with the jadwah of 28:29 and distinguishes it from an ember. Bint al-Shāṭiʾ contrasts its guiding warmth with hostile meteors and notes iqtabasa at 57:13; a report from al-Bāqir says the family needed warmth."}, {"id": "20:10/q14/p2", "position": "An ember or piece of fire to carry back.", "reasons": "Al-Bayḍāwī and al-Nasafī allow an ember, and Ibn Kathīr cites 28:29 for a glowing brand and warmth; Iṣlāḥī likewise speaks of an ember against cold."}]}
{"id": "20:10/q15", "question": "How do the related verbs for taking or giving fire and knowledge differ?", "turns_on": "Whether usage assigns separate domains to the simple and prefixed forms or allows both in both domains.", "positions": [{"id": "20:10/q15/p1", "position": "The simple form concerns fire; the prefixed form concerns seeking or imparting knowledge.", "reasons": "Abū Zayd distinguishes bringing fire from seeking it; al-Mubarrad and al-Samīn distinguish giving fire from giving knowledge. These reports differ in their precise formulation."}, {"id": "20:10/q15/p2", "position": "Both forms can be used for fire or knowledge.", "reasons": "Al-Kisāʾī allows both; al-Mubarrad says their underlying sense is one because both fire and knowledge illuminate."}]}
{"id": "20:10/q16", "question": "How is 'from it' attached grammatically?", "turns_on": "Direct verbal attachment or an omitted circumstance describing the brand.", "positions": [{"id": "20:10/q16/p1", "position": "It attaches directly to the verb 'bring'.", "reasons": "Al-Samīn and Abū al-Baqāʾ, as cited by al-Ālūsī, permit this attachment."}, {"id": "20:10/q16/p2", "position": "It is an omitted circumstantial qualification of the firebrand.", "reasons": "Al-Samīn and Abū al-Baqāʾ supply the omitted circumstance."}]}
{"id": "20:10/q17", "question": "Do the two hopes joined by 'or' exclude one another?", "turns_on": "Whether the alternatives are merely listed as possibilities or explicitly compatible.", "positions": [{"id": "20:10/q17/p1", "position": "They are alternative hoped-for outcomes but need not exclude obtaining both.", "reasons": "Bursevī explicitly allows both; al-Ālūsī says aw prevents exclusion and presents two anticipated possibilities."}, {"id": "20:10/q17/p2", "position": "They express two possible outcomes, neither yet certain.", "reasons": "Al-Ālūsī treats aw in the hope clause as the expression of two anticipated possibilities."}]}
{"id": "20:10/q18", "question": "What does 'upon the fire' mean?", "turns_on": "Whether ʿalā retains spatial elevation, stands for another local preposition, or describes an implicit guide.", "positions": [{"id": "20:10/q18/p1", "position": "On or above a nearby elevated place by the fire.", "reasons": "Al-Rāzī says people around a fire stand on overlooking ground; Abū Ḥayyān keeps the ordinary elevation sense, and al-Bayḍāwī and al-Nasafī allow elevated ground. Al-Ālūsī says elevation becomes an idiom for a nearby place, citing Sībawayh's account of bi as contact with a nearby place."}, {"id": "20:10/q18/p2", "position": "It means 'at,' 'with,' or 'by' the fire.", "reasons": "Ibn al-Anbārī offers these prepositional senses; al-Ālūsī says substitution is unnecessary."}, {"id": "20:10/q18/p3", "position": "It is a circumstance of an implied guide located near the fire.", "reasons": "Some grammarians move a description before its noun and take the result to mean someone near the fire who could help the family warm itself."}]}

{"id": "2:283/q49", "question": "What rhetorical qualities does Jurjani illustrate?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "2:283/q49/p1", "position": "Clear expression guides thought, while subtle rhetorical reversals join unlike ideas into a coherent point.", "reasons": "Jurjani contrasts opaque and clear paths, intellectual discovery and competition, then analyzes a poem's two hands and blameworthy withholding recast as benefit; al-Marzubani credits al-Khalil, and Abu al-Atahiya supplies an example."}]}
{"id": "2:283/q50", "question": "What examples illustrate semantic feminine agreement?", "turns_on": "These are auxiliary grammatical observations, each grounded in its own example.", "positions": [{"id": "2:283/q50/p1", "position": "Feminine verbal agreement may follow an understood feminine referent.", "reasons": "Farra cites تكون ميتة, إن تك مثقال حبة and poetry involving hand, death or hooked sticks."}]}
{"id": "2:283/q51", "question": "What auxiliary orthographic and particle rules are cited?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "2:283/q51/p1", "position": "A feminine tāʾ is written closed for name or quality and open when showing an act or effect.", "reasons": "Burhan describes the orthographic distinction."}, {"id": "2:283/q51/p2", "position": "An open-hamza an governs a subjunctive verb and its clause can fill several syntactic roles.", "reasons": "Burhan also notes conditional examples where surface condition is implausible."}]}
{"id": "2:283/q52", "question": "How do other verses express care of entrusted things?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "2:283/q52/p1", "position": "Riyāʿa denotes active, constant care of remote trusts, beyond simple keeping.", "reasons": "Samarrai cites Ruh al-Maʿani on shepherding and applies it to dependents, subjects, crops, livestock and religious obligations; the noun rāʿūn implies continuity, contrasting chastity kept with the person."}]}
{"id": "2:283/q53", "question": "What did a report say about knowledge?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "2:283/q53/p1", "position": "Knowledge sustains faith; one who learns and acts is taught more by God.", "reasons": "Durr transmits the report from Ibn Abbas ascribed to the Prophet."}]}
{"id": "2:283/q54", "question": "How does God know concealed and disclosed acts?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "2:283/q54/p1", "position": "He knows them through His essential knowledge, from which nothing is hidden.", "reasons": "Jishumi says God knows concealment and disclosure by virtue of His essential knowledge and that nothing escapes Him."}]}
{"id": "2:283/q55", "question": "How are the future forms of ḥasiba read in the cited recitation survey?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "2:283/q55/p1", "position": "Abu Ja'far, Ibn Amir, Asim and Hamza read the sin with fatḥa; the other readers use kasra.", "reasons": "Nashr states the rule for future forms such as taḥsab and yaḥsabanna wherever they occur."}]}
{"id": "20:10/q01", "question": "How does the time clause 'when he saw' connect grammatically to the account?", "turns_on": "Whether the preceding account has enough event sense to govern idh, or an unspoken command or event must be supplied.", "positions": [{"id": "20:10/q01/p1", "position": "It modifies the preceding account or report of Moses.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAṭiyya supplies the implicit action in ḥadīth; al-Ṭabrisī calls it an accusative circumstance; al-Bayḍāwī and Abū Ḥayyān treat the account as an event; al-Sharīf says story and report imply occurrence; al-Ālūsī prefers attachment to the preceding revealed account, since a bare substantive cannot govern the clause."}, {"id": "20:10/q01/p2", "position": "It is the object of an implicit command to remember the time.", "reasons": "Abū al-Baqāʾ and al-Zamakhsharī are cited for the implied udhkur; al-Bayḍāwī and al-Nasafī allow it."}, {"id": "20:10/q01/p3", "position": "It depends on an omitted following event or verb.", "reasons": "Al-Zamakhsharī is cited by al-Samīn and al-Ālūsī; al-Nasafī permits an omitted event."}]}
{"id": "20:10/q02", "question": "What journey and circumstances led Moses to see the fire?", "turns_on": "The reports differ in how Moses lost the road and in the journey's particular circumstances.", "positions": [{"id": "20:10/q02/p1", "position": "Returning from Midian toward Egypt with his family, Moses lost the way on a cold dark night and could not kindle fire.", "reasons": "Muqātil and others specify winter, sometimes Friday, snow, pregnancy or a son's birth, dispersed livestock, no water, and fire to the left or on a mountain near Ṭuwā. Wahb says Shuʿayb allowed a visit to Moses' mother; some mention Aaron, the completed term, a flock and more than ten years away. Ibn Kathīr cites 28:29; al-Kuranyolu gives eight or ten years. The reports vary in these details."}, {"id": "20:10/q02/p2", "position": "His protectiveness toward his wife led him to separate from companions and lose the route.", "reasons": "ʿAṭāʾ from Ibn ʿAbbās says he avoided a group lest they see her; al-Baghawī says he joined caravans at night and separated by day; al-Qurṭubī says God decreed the separation. Some add detouring from Syrian rulers."}, {"id": "20:10/q02/p3", "position": "The fire episode belongs to Moses' wanderings after fleeing Egypt.", "reasons": "Asad cites the sequence beginning at 28:14 and infers from 27:7 and 28:29 that Moses was lost in the desert."}]}
{"id": "20:10/q03", "question": "What did Moses actually see when the verse calls it fire?", "turns_on": "Whether 'fire' names a physical fire, divine light perceived as fire, a small visible flame, or an allegorical image; al-Rāzī and Bursevī appeal to prophetic truthfulness.", "positions": [{"id": "20:10/q03/p1", "position": "He saw divine light that appeared to him to be fire.", "reasons": "Al-Suddī, Ibn ʿAbbās and most exegetes distinguish Moses' perception from God's light; some call it the Lord's light. Al-Kuranyolu says the light drew him into God's presence. Al-Rāzī and Abū Ḥayyān object that making it merely imagined fire threatens the truth of a prophet's report."}, {"id": "20:10/q03/p2", "position": "It was real fire.", "reasons": "Saʿīd ibn Jubayr calls it one of God's veils and cites Abū Mūsā's report that the unveiled fire would burn creation within God's sight. Al-Rāzī and Bursevī prefer actual fire because prophets cannot lie; al-Rāzī says the verse does not establish that it was in a tree. Classifications distinguish Moses' fire as consuming neither food nor drink, or as luminous without burning, against worldly and infernal fires; 36:80 is cited."}, {"id": "20:10/q03/p3", "position": "He saw a brief shimmering flame, perhaps visible only to him.", "reasons": "Iṣlāḥī reasons that a large blaze would have prompted a different description; Ṭabāṭabāʾ takes the emphatic report to imply that only Moses perceived it."}, {"id": "20:10/q03/p4", "position": "The fire is an allegory of the burning bush.", "reasons": "Asad refers to the biblical burning bush and his note on 27:7–8."}]}
{"id": "20:10/q04", "question": "What was reported about the tree and fire as Moses approached?", "turns_on": "Reports give different tree species and details of its behavior; al-Rāzī questions whether the Qurʾānic wording establishes any tree.", "positions": [{"id": "20:10/q04/p1", "position": "The fire appeared in a green tree and did not consume it.", "reasons": "Al-Baghawī describes brilliant white fire surrounding the tree from bottom to top without altering its green color; Ibn ʿAbbās marveled at its unchanged beauty. Al-Mahdawī says it receded as Moses approached, then drew near after fear. Al-Qushayrī says the tree burned end to end but yielded no flame and illuminated hearts, while al-Rāzī notes the Qurʾān does not establish the tree detail."}, {"id": "20:10/q04/p2", "position": "The tree was a jujube or ʿanāb.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAbbās is reported for the jujube identification; Abū Ḥayyān's collected variants include ʿanāb."}, {"id": "20:10/q04/p3", "position": "The tree was al-ʿawsaj, a thorn tree.", "reasons": "Qatāda, Muqātil and al-Kalbī are named by al-Baghawī; al-Mahdawī says a thorn tree."}, {"id": "20:10/q04/p4", "position": "The tree was a green samura.", "reasons": "Al-Baghawī attributes this to Ibn Masʿūd; Abū Ḥayyān lists it among variants."}, {"id": "20:10/q04/p5", "position": "The tree was al-ʿaliq or ʿalīqah.", "reasons": "Al-Baghawī reports Wahb's identification; Abū Ḥayyān lists the variant."}, {"id": "20:10/q04/p6", "position": "Moses thought the distant light was a shepherd's fire.", "reasons": "Al-Suddī and Bursevī connect the expectation of a firebrand to shepherds."}]}
{"id": "20:10/q05", "question": "Who was Moses' 'family' whom he addressed?", "turns_on": "Whether ahl includes children and a servant, or denotes the wife alone with plural wording.", "positions": [{"id": "20:10/q05/p1", "position": "His wife, children, and possibly a servant.", "reasons": "Al-Rāzī gives wife, child and servant; Abū Ḥayyān specifies wife, two sons and servant. Al-Ālūsī allows wife, child and servant. Ṭabāṭabāʾ infers others were present from the instruction to stay."}, {"id": "20:10/q05/p2", "position": "His wife alone, Shuʿayb's daughter.", "reasons": "Al-Wāḥidī explains the plural by ahl's collective outward form; al-Rāzī and al-Ālūsī add respectful plural address. Al-Suhaylī names her Ṣafūriyya."}]}
{"id": "20:10/q06", "question": "What does 'stay' mean here?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "20:10/q06/p1", "position": "Remain here temporarily.", "reasons": "Al-Māwardī, al-Ṭabrisī and al-Qurṭubī distinguish makth from iqāma, which implies continuing residence; other sources gloss it as stay or remain in place.
